title: FATHERS DAY TORNADOES
full_story:
Father’s Day may have started bright but ended with a number of tornadoes and heavy rain in Clay County.

At about 1:30 pm the National Weather Service issued a tornado watch for much of southern Illinois, about 2 hours later a tornado warning was issued for Louisville and Sailor Springs.  At 3:39 the national weather service confirmed a tornado touchdown in Louisville.  The National weather service also reported a rotating wall cloud west of Clay City at about 5 pm but no touchdown was reported.

Steve Lewis with Clay County ESDA reports that one home was damaged northeast of Louisville.  The road was closed as crews repaired the power lines.  The Zimmerman transportation building sustained some damage and tree damage was reported throughout the county.

Jefferson County Sherrif Jeff Bullard says two people died in separate homes and both of the structures they were in were leveled.  He also reports that 5 other were injured and taken to the hospital.  At least three homes were completely leveled, and several others sustained significant damage.  The names of those deceased are not being released at this time, pending notification of their family members

title: MITIGATION PLANNING COMMITTEE MEETING
full_story:
The frequency of severe weather events and damages caused by them and other natural hazards will be discussed when the Clay County Hazard Mitigation Planning Committee meets at the Clay County Health Department, in Flora, at 1 pm today.

This Committee is comprised of County, municipal, healthcare, education, fire protection district, and emergency services representatives, as well as technical partners and stakeholders, will meet over the next several months to update the Clay County Natural Hazards Mitigation Plan.  All Committee meetings are open to the public.

“The goal of this Committee meeting is to identify how often severe weather events occur within the County and what kinds of damages have resulted.  Based on this information the committee will compile lists of activities and projects to reduce damages caused by these events,” said Steve Lewis, Flora-Clay County Emergency Services and Disaster Agency Coordinator.

The focus of this effort is on natural hazards, severe thunderstorms with damaging winds or hail, tornadoes, snow and ice storms, floods, drought, extreme cold, and excessive heat.  Interested persons can provide input at these Planning Committee meetings or submit their comments and questions to their municipal or County representatives.

Participants to date include the County, four municipalities, 10 townships, two school districts, three fire protection districts, the Clay Electric Cooperative, Clay County Water, and Clay County Hospital.  Jurisdictions who have yet to participate in a committee meeting are strongly encouraged to attend this meeting.

“This Plan will be our best resource for determining how to mitigate damages from storms and other natural hazards.  After the Plan is updated, comprehensive information will be available in one document to help guide those who are making decisions about how to better protect residents,” added Lewis.

title: CCH SPORTS PHYSICALS
full_story:
The Clay County Hospital is offering free sports physicals for the next school year.

The first opportunity for a free sports physical is on Wednesday at the Clay City Clinic.  The next happens on Wednesday, July 8th at the Flora Clinic, then Wednesday July 9th at the Louisville Clinic and finally Tuesday, July 14th at the Flora Clinic.  All clinics are from 4 to 6 pm.  Wabash General Hospital athletic trainers will be at the clinics to assess athlete’s injury risk.

Appointments are not needed; physicals will be done on a first-come first-serve basis.  Sports physicals do not qualify as school physicals.

title: OCC MASSAGE THERAPY SIGN UP
full_story:
Olney Central College’s Massage Therapy Program is accepting new students for Fall 2026.

Designed with busy adults in mind, the program offers convenient evening classes that allow students to pursue a rewarding new career without putting life on hold.  Best of all, the certificate can be completed in just one year.

While enrolled, students gain the skills needed to work in the wellness field of massage therapy, mastering professional massage techniques through hands-on classroom instruction and clinical experience. The program’s clinical opportunities, which are open to the public, provide students with valuable practice working with a variety of clients in a real-world setting.

Olney Central College is recognized as a National Certification Board for Therapeutic Massage & Bodywork (NCBTMB) Assigned School.  This designation confirms that OCC’s Massage Therapy Program meets the high standards of excellence established by the NCBTMB.  It also ensures that after successfully completing state licensure requirements, graduates are eligible to pursue NCBTMB board certification; the highest credential available in the massage therapy profession.

Enrollment is limited.  To reserve a spot, apply by July 15th at www.iecc.edu/apply.

title: FCC 3 on 3 TOURNAMENT
full_story:
Frontier Community College will continue celebrating its 50th anniversary with a 3-on-3 Basketball Tournament on Saturday, August 15th, at 10 am.  The tournament will be held in the Student Services Parking Lot on FCC’s campus.

The event will feature three age divisions: junior high for students in sixth through eighth grade, high school for students in ninth through 12th grade, and an adult division for participants 18 and older.

Teams may include up to four players and will compete in a double-elimination tournament format.  The team fee is $60.

The tournament is part of Frontier Community College’s ongoing 50th anniversary celebration and provides an opportunity for students, alumni, families, and community members to enjoy a fun day of basketball and Bobcat spirit.

For more information or to register a team, contact Frontier Community College at 618-842-3711.

title: GIANNOULIAS ENDS ROAD TESTS FOR SENIORS
full_story:
A major component of Secretary of State Alexi Giannoulias’ Road Safety & Fairness Act will begin next month with the elimination of the state’s mandatory behind-the-wheel driving tests for Illinois drivers ages 79 to 86.

Starting July 1st, the new law raises the age at which Illinois drivers must take a driving test from 79 to 87, removing an outdated age-based requirement that made Illinois the only state in the nation to require a behind-the-wheel test solely because of a driver’s age.

Instead, the new law shifts the focus to a person’s ability to drive safely; rather than the date of their birth certificate, Giannoulias said.

“The Road Safety & Fairness Act is about replacing outdated assumptions with facts,” Giannoulias said.  “Illinois seniors have consistently proven they are among the safest drivers on our roads.  This law removes an unnecessary burden for older drivers while preserving strong safeguards to protect everyone who travels on our streets.”

Under the Road Safety & Fairness Act, drivers ages 79 through 86 will still be required to renew their licenses in person at a DMV and pass a vision screening but will no longer be required to take a behind-the-wheel driving test solely because of their age.

The law does not change requirements for commercial driver’s license (CDL) holders, who must continue taking a behind-the-wheel driving test beginning at age 75 and at each subsequent renewal.

Importantly, the law strengthens road safety by creating a new process that allows immediate family members to report legitimate concerns when a loved one’s medical condition, vision impairment or driving behavior may affect their ability to drive safely.  Any report is independently reviewed by the Secretary of State’s office and a driver’s license is not automatically affected simply because a report is submitted.
